title: KV workload synthesis & load-harness for throughput/p95 regression detection
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: build a repeatable, CI-friendly load harness that synthesizes realistic KV and prefix-cache access patterns and produces token/sec, p95, and memory curves across hit-rate sweeps. This harness must run in nightly CI and as an ad-hoc perf job, produce deterministic samples (seeded RNG), and support multiple workload profiles: short-chat (seq len 64), long-dialog (seq len 1024), and mixed multi-turn. Outputs must ship to the benchmarks dashboard and create automated regression alerts when core metrics degrade relative to a certified baseline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can replay 3 workload profiles with configurable hit-rate targets (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%) and seedable RNG
2) Produces per-run metrics: aggregate tokens/sec, moving-window p50/p90/p95 latencies, 95th-tail per-batch latency, peak and resident memory (RSS), and cache footprint
3) Nightly CI integration: runs on dedicated perf infra, stores artifacts in s3://redwood-benchmarks/kv-harness/<date>/, and pushes summary to Grafana dashboard
4) Regression detection rules deployed: alert if tokens/sec drops >15% vs baseline for 3 consecutive nightly runs OR p95 increases >20% for 3 consecutive runs
5) Baseline snapshot tooling: harness can snapshot and compare to golden baselines, with diffable CSV and a human-readable summary
6) Documentation: README with run commands, config knobs (batch_size, seq_len_dist, kv_eviction_policy), and instructions for adding new workload profiles
notes: 2026-03-02: Spike completed. Implemented workload synthesizer that can emit key-access sequences sampled from a Zipf distribution and prefix expansions for realistic prefix-cache collisions.
2026-03-04: Prototype run on t4.xlarge perf cluster. Observed expected trade-offs: higher prefix hit-rate increases cache memory but reduces p95 latency and raises tokens/sec for short sequences.

2026-03-05: Trade-off discussion with runtime team: two approaches for CI execution -> (A) run full sweep nightly (longer, more stable) vs (B) run delta-only against changed model/runtime (faster). We decided to start with (A) for first 2 weeks, then shift to (B) for PR gating.
2026-03-06: Marco implemented atomic artifact uploads. Using S3 path convention and signed metadata file to ensure reproducibility.
2026-03-07: First formal run results attached below. Need to validate measurement noise and increase sample counts for 99% confidence on p95 estimates for low-throughput configs.

2026-03-09: Design review with PM and Observability team. Agreed to push summaries to Grafana and keep raw traces for 14 days. Also approved regression thresholds above; PM asked to revisit thresholds after 2 weeks of nightly data.
2026-03-10: Preparing PR to add harness job to nightly CI and a separate optional job for PRs that runs a smaller delta suite. Follow-ups listed in open_tasks below.
